m-iskanderkul.title: A turquoise mountain lake
m-iskanderkul.alt: A bright turquoise lake winding between steep, bare mountain slopes in shades of red, grey and green.
m-iskanderkul.clue: A turquoise lake in the Fann Mountains, in a small mountain country north of Afghanistan.
m-iskanderkul.story: The Fann Mountains in Tajikistan are dotted with turquoise lakes. Legend says nearby Iskanderkul is named after Alexander the Great.

m-wadirum.title: Red sand and rock
m-wadirum.alt: Huge red sandstone rock formations rising from orange desert sand under a clear blue sky.
m-wadirum.clue: A 'Valley of the Moon' of red sand and towering sandstone, north of the Red Sea, where many films set on Mars are shot.
m-wadirum.story: Wadi Rum in Jordan is a protected desert of sandstone and granite. Bedouin families have lived there for centuries.

m-banaue.title: A village in the terraces
m-banaue.alt: A small village of houses with red and silver roofs among curving, flooded rice terraces climbing a mountainside.
m-banaue.clue: Rice terraces carved into mountains by the Ifugao people about 2,000 years ago, on a northern island of a country of 7,000 islands.
m-banaue.story: The Batad rice terraces near Banaue in the Philippines form a giant amphitheatre. They are still farmed by hand.

m-gardensbay.title: A steel supertree
m-gardensbay.alt: Looking up at a giant steel tree-like tower with a crown of branching metal arms against a cloudy sky.
m-gardensbay.clue: Giant steel 'supertrees' covered in plants, in a garden on reclaimed land in a small island city-state near the equator.
m-gardensbay.story: The Supertree Grove at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore opened in 2012. The trees are up to 50 metres tall and light up in a show every evening.

m-hunza.title: A valley of poplars
m-hunza.alt: A green valley of poplar trees and terraced fields beside a winding river, surrounded by bare brown mountains and snowy peaks.
m-hunza.clue: A green valley of apricot orchards and poplars on the old Silk Road, ringed by some of the highest peaks of the Karakoram.
m-hunza.story: The Hunza Valley in Pakistan lies along the Karakoram Highway. Its villages are famous for apricots and for views of Rakaposhi, over 7,700 metres tall.

m-gobi.title: Singing dunes
m-gobi.alt: Long pale sand dunes stretching to the horizon beside a strip of green grass, under a blue sky with small clouds.
m-gobi.clue: Huge 'singing' sand dunes in a cold desert in the south of a land of nomads, horses and round felt tents.
m-gobi.story: Khongoryn Els in Mongolia's Gobi Desert stretches for about 180 kilometres. The dunes hum when the wind moves the sand.

m-ella.title: A bridge of nine arches
m-ella.alt: A curving stone railway bridge of tall arches crossing a valley thick with jungle.
m-ella.clue: A railway viaduct of nine stone arches in the green hill country of a teardrop-shaped island famous for tea.
m-ella.story: The Nine Arch Bridge near Ella in Sri Lanka was finished in 1921 and is built of stone, brick and cement without steel. Blue trains cross it several times a day.

m-plitvice.title: Waterfalls into turquoise
m-plitvice.alt: Dozens of thin waterfalls pouring down a mossy green cliff into a clear turquoise pool.
m-plitvice.clue: Sixteen terraced lakes joined by waterfalls, in a forest park in the hills near the Adriatic coast.
m-plitvice.story: The Plitvice Lakes in Croatia are separated by natural dams of travertine that grow a little every year. Wooden boardwalks run right over the water.

m-positano.title: A village on a cliff
m-positano.alt: Pastel houses stacked steeply up a hillside above the sea, seen from a terrace with pots of lemons.
m-positano.clue: Pastel houses tumbling down a cliff to the sea, on a coast famous for lemons and winding roads south of Naples.
m-positano.story: Positano on the Amalfi Coast of Italy was once a poor fishing village. Today its steep lanes are mostly stairs, and lemons grown nearby are made into limoncello.

m-colmar.title: Half-timbered houses by a canal
m-colmar.alt: Colourful half-timbered houses with flower boxes lining a still canal, reflected in the water.
m-colmar.clue: Painted half-timbered houses along a canal nicknamed 'Little Venice', in a wine region on a river border with its eastern neighbour.
m-colmar.story: Colmar in Alsace, France, is known for its old houses and canals. The Statue of Liberty's sculptor, Auguste Bartholdi, was born there.

m-lofoten.title: A fishing village under peaks
m-lofoten.alt: Red and white wooden houses along the shore of a still bay, beneath jagged rocky mountains.
m-lofoten.clue: Red fishing cabins under jagged peaks on islands far above the Arctic Circle, where cod is dried on wooden racks.
m-lofoten.story: Reine is a fishing village in the Lofoten Islands of Norway. In summer the sun never sets there, and in winter the northern lights appear.

m-ronda.title: A bridge over a gorge
m-ronda.alt: A tall stone bridge spanning a deep gorge between sheer cliffs, with white buildings perched on the edge.
m-ronda.clue: A town split by a deep gorge and joined by an 18th-century stone bridge, in the hills of the south, birthplace of modern bullfighting.
m-ronda.story: The Puente Nuevo in Ronda, Spain, was finished in 1793 and stands about 98 metres above the river. It took over 40 years to build.

m-krumlov.title: A castle tower above a river
m-krumlov.alt: A painted castle tower and red roofs above a wide shallow river with a wooden bridge and colourful houses.
m-krumlov.clue: A painted castle tower above a bend of the Vltava, in a small medieval town in the south of a country in the heart of Europe.
m-krumlov.story: Český Krumlov in the Czech Republic has a castle that is the second largest in the country. Its old town has hardly changed since the 1700s.

m-sighisoara.title: A cobbled old street
m-sighisoara.alt: A quiet cobbled lane between brightly painted houses in orange, green and yellow, with wooden shutters.
m-sighisoara.clue: Painted houses in a hilltop citadel in Transylvania, where a famous 15th-century prince was said to have been born.
m-sighisoara.story: Sighișoara in Romania is one of the last lived-in medieval citadels in Europe. Vlad the Impaler, who inspired Dracula, was born there.

m-giants.title: Stepping stones of a giant
m-giants.alt: Thousands of six-sided stone columns stepping down into a wild blue sea, with walkers on the cliffs.
m-giants.clue: About 40,000 six-sided basalt columns by the sea, said in legend to be stepping stones built by a giant to cross to Scotland.
m-giants.story: The Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland formed when lava cooled and cracked about 50 million years ago. Most of the columns are hexagons.

m-rainbow.title: A mountain of stripes
m-rainbow.alt: A mountain ridge striped in bands of red, purple, cream and green, with hikers resting at the top.
m-rainbow.clue: A mountain striped like a rainbow by minerals, high in the Andes above 5,000 metres, near the old Inca capital.
m-rainbow.story: Vinicunca, the Rainbow Mountain in Peru, was covered by ice until recent decades. Its colours come from minerals such as iron oxide.

m-antigua.title: An arch below a volcano
m-antigua.alt: A yellow arch with a clock tower over a cobbled street of colourful houses, with a large volcano behind.
m-antigua.clue: A yellow arch across a cobbled street in an old colonial capital ringed by three volcanoes in Central America.
m-antigua.story: The Santa Catalina Arch in Antigua Guatemala was built in the 1600s so nuns could cross the street unseen. The Volcán de Agua rises behind it.

m-antelope.title: A canyon of waves
m-antelope.alt: Looking up through a narrow slot canyon of smooth, flowing red sandstone walls to a strip of blue sky.
m-antelope.clue: A slot canyon of smooth wave-shaped red sandstone, carved by flash floods on Navajo land in the south-west.
m-antelope.story: Antelope Canyon in Arizona can only be visited with a Navajo guide. Sunbeams shine down into it at midday in summer.

m-pelourinho.title: A colonial square
m-pelourinho.alt: A sloping cobbled square with colourful colonial buildings, a large sky-blue one in the middle, and people strolling.
m-pelourinho.clue: A sloping square of colourful colonial buildings in the old centre of the first capital of a huge South American country.
m-pelourinho.story: Pelourinho is the historic centre of Salvador, Brazil. The city's African heritage lives on in its music, food and capoeira.

m-cocora.title: The tallest palms
m-cocora.alt: Very tall, thin palm trees standing on a bright green hillside, fading into the mist.
m-cocora.clue: The world's tallest palm trees, up to 60 metres high, in a misty valley of the coffee-growing Andes.
m-cocora.story: The Cocora Valley in Colombia is home to the Quindío wax palm, the national tree. The palms can live for more than a hundred years.

m-quilotoa.title: A lake in a crater
m-quilotoa.alt: A large green-blue lake filling a deep volcanic crater, ringed by steep slopes under a sky of big white clouds.
m-quilotoa.clue: A water-filled volcanic crater high in the Andes, on a hiking loop through Kichwa villages on the equator's line of volcanoes.
m-quilotoa.story: Quilotoa in Ecuador is a crater lake about three kilometres wide, formed when a volcano collapsed some 800 years ago. Minerals turn the water green and blue.

m-atacama.title: The Valley of the Moon
m-atacama.alt: A dry valley of pale sand, salt crusts and eroded rock ridges, with a great sandstone wall like an amphitheatre behind.
m-atacama.clue: A 'Valley of the Moon' of salt and sand in the driest non-polar desert on Earth, high on a long Pacific coast.
m-atacama.story: Valle de la Luna lies near San Pedro de Atacama in Chile. Some weather stations in the Atacama Desert have never recorded rain.

m-tulum.title: Ruins above a Caribbean beach
m-tulum.alt: A small stone temple on a rocky headland above a white beach and bright turquoise sea, framed by palm trees.
m-tulum.clue: A walled Maya city on a cliff above the Caribbean Sea, one of the last the Maya built and lived in.
m-tulum.story: Tulum on the Yucatán Peninsula of Mexico was a busy Maya port around 1200 to 1500. The small Temple of the God of the Winds stands right above the sea.

m-aitbenhaddou.title: Camels by a mud-brick village
m-aitbenhaddou.alt: Two pale camels nose to nose in front of the towers and walls of a village built of red earth, among palm trees.
m-aitbenhaddou.clue: A fortified village of red earth on an old caravan route over the Atlas Mountains, seen in many films.
m-aitbenhaddou.story: Aït Benhaddou in Morocco is a ksar, a group of earthen buildings behind high walls. Its walls are repaired with mud after the winter rains.

m-tsingy.title: A forest of stone needles
m-tsingy.alt: A landscape of sharp grey limestone pinnacles packed tightly together, with a strip of green forest beyond.
m-tsingy.clue: A 'forest' of razor-sharp limestone needles on a large island off south-east Africa, home of lemurs.
m-tsingy.story: Tsingy de Bemaraha in Madagascar gets its name from a Malagasy word meaning 'where one cannot walk barefoot'. Rope bridges cross between the pinnacles.

m-ghardaia.title: A desert town on a hill
m-ghardaia.alt: A dense town of pale, flat-roofed houses climbing a low hill in a dry red-brown valley, with a minaret at the top.
m-ghardaia.clue: Five fortified hill towns in a valley of the Sahara, whose simple cube houses inspired modern architects.
m-ghardaia.story: Ghardaïa in Algeria is one of the towns of the M'zab valley, founded about a thousand years ago. The architect Le Corbusier admired its plain houses.

m-capecoast.title: A white castle by the sea
m-capecoast.alt: A large whitewashed castle courtyard with a double staircase, old cannons and cannonballs, under a hazy sky.
m-capecoast.clue: A whitewashed castle on the Gulf of Guinea, a sad reminder of the Atlantic slave trade on the old Gold Coast.
m-capecoast.story: Cape Coast Castle in Ghana was built by European traders in the 1600s. Today it is a museum that remembers the people held there.

m-reef.title: A reef from the air
m-reef.alt: Seen from a plane: turquoise shallows, dark patches of coral and a small white sand island in a deep blue sea.
m-reef.clue: The largest coral reef system in the world, so big it can be seen from space, off a north-eastern coast.
m-reef.story: The Great Barrier Reef off Queensland, Australia, stretches for about 2,300 kilometres. It is made of nearly 3,000 separate reefs.

m-tongariro.title: Emerald lakes
m-tongariro.alt: Bright green crater lakes below steaming volcanic slopes of dark rock and red earth.
m-tongariro.clue: Bright green crater lakes on a famous volcanic day hike, in a volcanic park sacred to the Māori people.
m-tongariro.story: The Emerald Lakes lie on the Tongariro Alpine Crossing in New Zealand. Their colour comes from minerals washed down from the volcano.

m-tosua.title: A swimming hole in the earth
m-tosua.alt: A deep round hole in the ground lined with ferns and vines, with a long wooden ladder down to clear green seawater.
m-tosua.clue: A giant swimming hole joined to the sea by a lava tube, on an island nation of the South Pacific.
m-tosua.story: To Sua Ocean Trench on Upolu, Samoa, is about 30 metres deep. Swimmers climb down a long wooden ladder to reach the water.

m-khiva.title: A forest of wooden pillars
m-khiva.alt: A prayer hall filled with rows of carved wooden columns under a flat timber ceiling, with light falling through an opening.
m-khiva.clue: A mosque hall of over 200 carved wooden pillars, inside the walled inner town of an old Silk Road oasis.
m-khiva.story: The Juma Mosque in Khiva, Uzbekistan, has 213 wooden columns; a few are about a thousand years old. Khiva's inner town, Itchan Kala, is ringed by mud-brick walls.

m-songkol.title: A horse by a high lake
m-songkol.alt: A dark horse standing on a wide grassy plain beside a big blue lake, with low mountains on the far shore.
m-songkol.clue: A high mountain lake where nomad herders bring their horses and set up felt yurts each summer, in the Tian Shan.
m-songkol.story: Song-Köl in Kyrgyzstan lies about 3,000 metres up. Its lakeside pastures are used only in summer; in winter the lake freezes over.

m-cameron.title: Hills of tea
m-cameron.alt: Rounded hills covered in neat rows of bright green tea bushes, with forest above and grey clouds.
m-cameron.clue: Tea gardens in cool highlands that colonial planters opened in the 1920s, a few hours from a tropical capital of twin towers.
m-cameron.story: The Cameron Highlands in Malaysia are about 1,500 metres up, cool enough for tea. Its plantations also grow strawberries and vegetables.

m-lencois.title: Sand and lagoons
m-lencois.alt: Seen from above: wide pale sand bars and shallow lagoons with patches of green scrub, stretching towards white dunes.
m-lencois.clue: White dunes and rainwater lagoons near the equator on an Atlantic coast, in a country famous for its rainforest.
m-lencois.story: The Lençóis Maranhenses in north-eastern Brazil fill with rain each year, making thousands of lagoons between the dunes. Fish appear in them every rainy season.

m-cinqueterre.title: Terraces above the sea
m-cinqueterre.alt: Steep hillside vineyards on stone terraces dropping to a deep blue sea, with coastal villages beyond.
m-cinqueterre.clue: Five fishing villages linked by footpaths along a steep coast of vineyards above the Ligurian Sea.
m-cinqueterre.story: The Cinque Terre villages lie on the Ligurian coast. Their dry-stone terraces stretch for thousands of kilometres and were built by hand over centuries.

m-peyto.title: A wolf-shaped lake
m-peyto.alt: A milky turquoise lake in a forested valley between grey mountains, under a sky of white clouds.
m-peyto.clue: A glacier-fed turquoise lake shaped like a wolf's head, high in the Rocky Mountains along the Icefields Parkway.
m-peyto.story: Peyto Lake in Banff National Park, Canada, gets its colour from rock flour carried in by glacier meltwater. It is named after an early mountain guide, Bill Peyto.

m-fitzroy.title: Granite spires over a lake
m-fitzroy.alt: Jagged granite spires capped with snow rising above green hills and a dark lake, in golden evening light.
m-fitzroy.clue: Jagged granite peaks on the Patagonian ice field, in a trekking village that calls itself the national capital of trekking.
m-fitzroy.story: Monte Fitz Roy in Argentina is 3,405 metres tall. The Tehuelche people called it Chaltén, the 'smoking mountain', because clouds often gather at its top.

m-lamu.title: An old Swahili town
m-lamu.alt: An old town of whitewashed stone houses and a mosque beside a waterfront full of small boats, seen from the air.
m-lamu.clue: An old Swahili stone town on an island in the Indian Ocean, where donkeys still carry goods because there are hardly any cars.
m-lamu.story: Lamu Old Town in Kenya is the oldest continuously lived-in Swahili town in East Africa. Dhows still sail from its harbour.

m-bandiagara.title: Granaries under a cliff
m-bandiagara.alt: Tall round and square mud-brick granaries and houses packed against the foot of a high sandstone cliff.
m-bandiagara.clue: Mud-brick villages and granaries built along a 150-kilometre cliff by the Dogon people, south of the great bend of the Niger.
m-bandiagara.story: The Bandiagara Escarpment in Mali is home to the Dogon, who have lived there since around the 14th century. Older cliff dwellings were built by the Tellem people before them.

m-bungle.title: Beehive domes
m-bungle.alt: A rounded rock dome striped in orange and grey bands like a beehive, with grass and pale trees at its base.
m-bungle.clue: Striped orange-and-black sandstone domes like giant beehives, in the remote north-west outback.
m-bungle.story: The Bungle Bungle Range in Purnululu National Park, Australia, was little known outside the area until the 1980s. The dark stripes are bacteria living in the rock.

t-kochinets.title: A fishing net at sunrise
t-kochinets.alt: A huge cantilevered fishing net on a wooden frame, lifted out of golden water at sunrise, with palm trees behind and birds flying.
t-kochinets.clue: Giant shore-operated fishing nets, said to have come with traders from the Far East, on the backwaters of a south-western coast of coconut palms.
t-kochinets.story: These Chinese fishing nets on Ashtamudi Lake in Kollam, Kerala, are worked by a team of fishermen using counterweights of stone. Kochi has the most famous row of them.

t-pushkar.title: An old herder at a camel fair
t-pushkar.alt: An old man with a white beard and a big pale turban leaning on a stick, with many camels resting on sandy ground behind him.
t-pushkar.clue: A giant turban and thousands of camels at a yearly desert fair beside a holy lake, in a north-western state of forts.
t-pushkar.story: The Pushkar Camel Fair in Rajasthan, India, brings thousands of camels, horses and cattle to the desert town every November. It ends with a full-moon bathing festival in the lake.

t-devaraja.title: A busy market gate
t-devaraja.alt: A crowded street full of parked scooters and market umbrellas in front of a long yellow colonial-style market building and a decorated clock tower.
t-devaraja.clue: Scooters, umbrellas and a pastel clock tower by an old market famous for jasmine, betel leaves and sandalwood, in a southern palace city.
t-devaraja.story: Devaraja Market in Mysuru, Karnataka, India, has been running for over 130 years. Its flower sellers stack marigolds and jasmine into tall, bright pyramids.

t-toytrain.title: A little blue mountain train
t-toytrain.alt: A small blue diesel locomotive pulling two blue carriages on narrow tracks beside a winding road through green forest.
t-toytrain.clue: A narrow-gauge 'toy train' that climbs to a hill station of tea gardens in the eastern Himalaya, sharing the road with cars.
t-toytrain.story: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway in West Bengal, India, opened in 1881. Its tracks are just 610 millimetres apart and loop and zigzag up the mountains.

t-amsterdam.title: A bike by a painted door
t-amsterdam.alt: A bicycle leaning on an old shopfront covered in colourful graffiti, with tall wooden doors and a brick pavement.
t-amsterdam.clue: Bicycles outnumber people in this canal city, where old merchant houses have narrow doors and big windows.
t-amsterdam.story: Amsterdam in the Netherlands has more bicycles than people, about 880,000 of them. Thousands are fished out of its canals every year.

t-paris.title: Teddy bears at a café
t-paris.alt: Giant teddy bears sitting at small marble tables on a café pavement, among woven bistro chairs, with a wide street behind.
t-paris.clue: Woven rattan bistro chairs facing the street, a café custom of a capital famous for its pavement terraces.
t-paris.story: These bears sat at a café in Paris's 6th arrondissement when cafés were closed during the pandemic. Paris cafés line their chairs up facing the street, so people can watch passers-by.

t-nyhavn.title: Painted houses by a harbour
t-nyhavn.alt: A row of tall, brightly painted gabled townhouses along a canal with old wooden sailing ships and crowded café tables.
t-nyhavn.clue: Brightly painted harbour houses and wooden ships, where a famous writer of fairy tales once lived, in a Nordic capital.
t-nyhavn.story: Nyhavn in Copenhagen, Denmark, was dug in the 1670s. Hans Christian Andersen lived in three of its houses.

t-helsinki.title: A tram in the snow
t-helsinki.alt: A dark tram curving through a snowy junction between tall city buildings, with cars and a few people under falling snow.
t-helsinki.clue: A tram on a snowy morning in a Nordic capital on the Baltic, where winters are long and saunas are everywhere.
t-helsinki.story: Helsinki in Finland has run electric trams since 1900. Finland has around three million saunas for about 5.6 million people.

t-prague.title: A red and cream tram
t-prague.alt: A red and cream tram with a pantograph on top, running on tracks beside a wide road, lit by low evening sun.
t-prague.clue: A red-and-cream tram of a design built in huge numbers nearby, in a 'city of a hundred spires' on the Vltava.
t-prague.story: Tatra T3 trams like this were built in Prague, Czech Republic, and over 13,000 were made. Prague still runs them on its streets.

t-sofia.title: A yellow tram on a leafy street
t-sofia.alt: A yellow two-car tram on tracks along a tree-lined street with parked cars and old apartment buildings.
t-sofia.clue: A yellow tram on a leafy street in a Balkan capital at the foot of Vitosha mountain, where signs are in Cyrillic.
t-sofia.story: Sofia in Bulgaria opened its first tram line in 1901. Bulgaria was the first country to use the Cyrillic alphabet officially.

t-lviv.title: Rooftops of an old town
t-lviv.alt: Old town rooftops in red and grey around a green-domed church and a square, seen from high above, with green hills beyond.
t-lviv.clue: Rooftops of an old town known for its coffee houses and chocolate, near the western border of the largest country entirely in Europe.
t-lviv.story: Lviv in western Ukraine has a historic centre on the World Heritage list. Its market square, Rynok, has 44 old houses around the town hall.

t-taipeinight.title: A night market
t-taipeinight.alt: A crowded night market street under glowing round lanterns with large characters, lit shop signs and food stalls.
t-taipeinight.clue: Lanterns and signs in traditional characters over a crowded night market, on an island famous for street snacks and bubble tea.
t-taipeinight.story: Linjiang Street Night Market in Taipei, Taiwan, is known for its food stalls. Taiwan's night markets started as places to eat and shop after the day's heat.

t-phnompenh.title: A tuk-tuk at the kerb
t-phnompenh.alt: A motorbike hitched to an orange covered passenger carriage with padded seats, parked by a leafy pavement with flowers.
t-phnompenh.clue: A motorbike pulling a covered trailer for passengers, the usual taxi in a riverside capital where the Mekong meets the Tonlé Sap.
t-phnompenh.story: In Phnom Penh, Cambodia, a 'remork' tuk-tuk is a motorbike towing a passenger carriage. Drivers often decorate their carriages.

t-jakarta.title: A row of orange three-wheelers
t-jakarta.alt: Several orange three-wheeled taxis with black canvas roofs parked in a row along a city street.
t-jakarta.clue: Orange three-wheeled 'bajaj' taxis, named after the company that first made them, on the streets of a huge capital on Java.
t-jakarta.story: Bajaj taxis have been part of Jakarta, Indonesia, since the 1970s. Newer blue ones run on natural gas.

t-kathmandu.title: Lighting butter lamps
t-kathmandu.alt: A woman in a blue top and orange scarf lighting rows of small brass oil lamps at a street shrine in a busy market.
t-kathmandu.clue: Butter lamps lit at a street shrine in an old bazaar of a Himalayan capital, where Hindu and Buddhist traditions mix.
t-kathmandu.story: Asan Tole is one of the oldest market squares in Kathmandu, Nepal. Its small Annapurna temple is busy with people lighting lamps all day.

t-tehran.title: A bazaar roof of stars
t-tehran.alt: Looking up at brick domes in a covered bazaar, patterned with intricate star shapes around small skylights.
t-tehran.clue: Brick domes patterned like stars over a covered bazaar, built by master builders of a land of old caravanserais.
t-tehran.story: This is the roof of the grand bazaar in Qom, Iran. Persian builders have made such patterned brick vaults, called muqarnas and karbandi, for centuries.

t-amman.title: A late-night shawarma shop
t-amman.alt: A brightly lit corner shop with a big Arabic sign, where people queue at the counter for sandwiches at night.
t-amman.clue: Arabic signs and a queue for shawarma in a capital built over seven hills, near the Dead Sea.
t-amman.story: Downtown Amman in Jordan is famous for cheap and busy food shops. The city was once called Philadelphia in Roman times.

t-doha.title: A stone souq
t-doha.alt: A long covered passage of rough stone walls with blue shutters and wooden beams poking out, seen from above.
t-doha.clue: A rebuilt old souq of mud and stone with wooden beams, in a Gulf capital on a small peninsula.
t-doha.story: Souq Waqif in Doha, Qatar, was rebuilt in 2006 in the old style. It sells spices, falcons and traditional clothes.

t-baku.title: A mosque in the old city
t-baku.alt: A sandstone mosque with a dome and a short round minaret beside a quiet street with parked cars and walkers.
t-baku.clue: A sandstone mosque inside the walled old city of a windy capital on the Caspian Sea.
t-baku.story: The Juma Mosque stands in Icherisheher, the old city of Baku, Azerbaijan. Baku's name is often said to mean 'city of winds'.

t-almaty.title: A trolleybus stop
t-almaty.alt: A blue and white trolleybus with a Cyrillic destination sign at a stop on a wide street lined with bare trees.
t-almaty.clue: A trolleybus with Cyrillic signs in a former capital at the foot of snowy mountains, famous for its apples.
t-almaty.story: Almaty was the capital of Kazakhstan until 1997. Its name is linked to the word for apple, and wild apples first grew in the hills around it.

t-bishkek.title: Felt slippers
t-bishkek.alt: A pile of handmade felt slippers, stitched with red and blue swirling patterns, on a market stall.
t-bishkek.clue: Felt slippers stitched with ram's-horn swirls in a bazaar of a mountain land whose flag shows a yurt's roof.
t-bishkek.story: Felt-making is an old craft in Kyrgyzstan, where nomads have long made yurts and rugs from sheep's wool. These were at the Osh Bazaar in Bishkek.

t-tashkent.title: An old van by a bazaar
t-tashkent.alt: An old red and white minibus with a flat front, parked by a pavement near market stalls and another yellow van.
t-tashkent.clue: A Soviet-era minibus near a great domed bazaar in the largest city of Central Asia.
t-tashkent.story: This old RAF van was parked near Chorsu Bazaar in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Tashkent rebuilt much of its centre after an earthquake in 1966.

t-dakar.title: A painted bus
t-dakar.alt: A blue, yellow and orange minibus with painted decorations and passengers at the windows, on a sandy roadside.
t-dakar.clue: A hand-painted 'car rapide' minibus, a symbol of a city on the westernmost point of mainland Africa.
t-dakar.story: The car rapide buses of Dakar, Senegal, are painted with bright colours and eyes to keep away bad luck. Newer buses are slowly replacing them.

t-kampala.title: A bike full of jerrycans
t-kampala.alt: A man pushing a bicycle loaded with dozens of yellow plastic jerrycans along a brick pavement beside a red-brick wall.
t-kampala.clue: A bicycle piled with yellow jerrycans in a hilly capital on the shores of Africa's largest lake.
t-kampala.story: Kampala in Uganda is built on hills near Lake Victoria. Bikes and boda-boda motorbikes carry all kinds of loads around the city.

t-kigali.title: A street of patterned dresses
t-kigali.alt: A shady street with a woman in a bright patterned dress holding a child's hand, motorbikes and parked cars, and clothes for sale.
t-kigali.clue: Motorbike taxis and bright wax-print dresses in a clean, hilly capital known as a 'land of a thousand hills'.
t-kigali.story: Kigali in Rwanda is known for its tidy streets; plastic bags have been banned there since 2008. On one Saturday each month, people do community work together.

t-tunis.title: A hat maker's shop
t-tunis.alt: An older man in a grey coat shaping red felt hats on a wooden table, with stacks of hats and boxes all around.
t-tunis.clue: Red felt chechia hats made by hand in a covered souk of a Mediterranean capital near the ruins of Carthage.
t-tunis.story: Chechia makers in the souk of Tunis, Tunisia, knit, felt, dye and brush each hat by hand. The craft came with Andalusian refugees in the 1600s.

t-madagascar.title: A zebu cart in a creek
t-madagascar.alt: A cart pulled by humped cattle wading along a shallow muddy creek between tall reeds and autumn-coloured trees.
t-madagascar.clue: Humped zebu cattle pulling a cart through water, on a huge island where these cattle are a sign of wealth.
t-madagascar.story: Zebu carts are a common way to carry goods in rural Madagascar. Families measure wealth in zebu, which are central to many ceremonies.

t-luxor.title: Sailboats on a wide river
t-luxor.alt: A crowd of white wooden sailboats with tall masts moored on a broad river, with a cruise ship and a green bank beyond.
t-luxor.clue: Wooden feluccas with tall masts waiting on a great river, in a city built on the site of ancient Thebes.
t-luxor.story: Feluccas have sailed the Nile for thousands of years. In Luxor, Egypt, they carry visitors between the temples on the east bank and the tombs on the west.

t-neworleans.title: A balcony party
t-neworleans.alt: Three men on an iron-railed balcony draped with ribbons and bead necklaces, laughing and waving under grey shutters.
t-neworleans.clue: Beads and ribbons on an iron balcony during a famous carnival in a jazz city on a great river delta.
t-neworleans.story: This photo shows Mardi Gras in the French Quarter of New Orleans, United States, in 1982. Throwing bead necklaces from balconies is a carnival tradition.

t-chickenbus.title: A painted bus
t-chickenbus.alt: A brightly painted old school bus in red and green with a chrome grille, parked on a dirt street by small shops in the hills.
t-chickenbus.clue: A retired school bus painted in bold colours, now a 'chicken bus' climbing the highland roads of Central America.
t-chickenbus.story: Guatemala's chicken buses are old school buses from the north, repainted and decorated. This one was in the mountain town of Zunil.

t-havanacar.title: A blue classic car
t-havanacar.alt: A sky-blue 1950s car parked in a lane of brightly painted houses covered in murals and metal sculptures.
t-havanacar.clue: A 1950s car parked in a lane full of Afro-Caribbean murals, in a capital on a big island south of Florida.
t-havanacar.story: Callejón de Hamel in Havana, Cuba, is an alley of murals and sculptures celebrating Afro-Cuban culture. Cuba is famous for its classic cars kept running for decades.

t-quito.title: An old street in the hills
t-quito.alt: A sloping colonial street with balconies, a yellow taxi, a red bus and a policeman in a yellow vest, with green mountains behind.
t-quito.clue: A colonial street with wrought-iron balconies in a high capital just south of the equator, ringed by volcanoes.
t-quito.story: This is a street in the old town of Quito, Ecuador, one of the first places named a World Heritage Site. Quito sits about 2,850 metres up.

t-laboca.title: A painted street corner
t-laboca.alt: A corner of colourful houses painted blue, yellow, green and red, with balconies, a mural and people strolling.
t-laboca.clue: Houses painted with leftover ship's paint in an old port barrio, home of the tango and a famous blue-and-gold football club.
t-laboca.story: Caminito in the La Boca neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, Argentina, was painted by dock workers' families with leftover paint. Tango dancers perform in its streets.

t-medellin.title: Cable cars over hillside homes
t-medellin.alt: Cable car cabins gliding above a hillside covered in red-brick houses, with green buses below and mountains behind.
t-medellin.clue: Cable cars run as public transport up to hillside neighbourhoods in a valley city once called the 'city of eternal spring'.
t-medellin.story: Medellín in Colombia opened its Metrocable in 2004 to link hillside neighbourhoods to the metro. It cut journeys from hours to minutes.

t-melbourne.title: A green tram
t-melbourne.alt: A long modern tram with a green pattern stopping on a busy city street beside old stone and new buildings.
t-melbourne.clue: A city with the largest tram network in the world, in the south-east of an island continent.
t-melbourne.story: Melbourne in Australia has about 250 kilometres of tram track, the largest network in the world. Trams in the city centre are free to ride.

t-chandnichowk.title: A spice market from above
t-chandnichowk.alt: Looking down on an old market courtyard with sacks and baskets of spices, men sitting on stools, blue tarpaulins and tangled wires.
t-chandnichowk.clue: Sacks of chillies and turmeric in a wholesale spice market in the lanes of an old walled Mughal city.
t-chandnichowk.story: Khari Baoli in Old Delhi, India, has been a spice market since the 1600s and is one of the largest in Asia. Its lanes run off Chandni Chowk.

t-flowermarket.title: Mountains of marigolds
t-flowermarket.alt: Huge sacks overflowing with orange and yellow marigolds on a market street, with a woman in a yellow sari walking past.
t-flowermarket.clue: Marigolds sold by the sackful for garlands, at a flower market by the bridge of a great eastern river city.
t-flowermarket.story: Mallick Ghat Flower Market in Kolkata, India, sits beside the Howrah Bridge on the Hooghly river. Over a century old, it sells flowers for weddings, festivals and temples.

t-assamtea.title: Picking tea
t-assamtea.alt: Three women with bright headscarves and wicker baskets on their backs picking leaves in a green tea garden under tall shade trees.
t-assamtea.clue: Tea pickers with baskets carried from the forehead, in the low, rainy Brahmaputra valley that grows a strong, malty tea.
t-assamtea.story: Assam in north-east India grows more tea than almost anywhere else on Earth. Shade trees protect the bushes, and pickers take 'two leaves and a bud'.

t-autorickshaw.title: A three-wheeler by a brick wall
t-autorickshaw.alt: A black and yellow three-wheeled auto rickshaw with a canvas roof and a driver inside, parked by an old red-brick wall.
t-autorickshaw.clue: A black-and-yellow three-wheeler with Devanagari lettering on its roof, the everyday taxi of a country of over a billion people.
t-autorickshaw.story: Auto rickshaws are the most common shared taxis in India. Most run on compressed natural gas in big cities to keep the air cleaner.

t-hongkongtram.title: Towers by the harbour
t-hongkongtram.alt: Very tall, slim apartment towers rising behind a curved modern station building with gardens and people walking.
t-hongkongtram.clue: Some of the tallest homes in the world, packed on reclaimed land beside a harbour, in a city that was a British colony until 1997.
t-hongkongtram.story: The Kowloon waterfront in Hong Kong, China, is built on land reclaimed from the sea. Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than any other city.

t-budapesttram.title: A yellow tram by the river
t-budapesttram.alt: A long yellow and white tram on a raised track beside a road, with green railings, trees and old buildings behind.
t-budapesttram.clue: A yellow tram running along the banks of the Danube, in a capital made of two old towns joined by bridges.
t-budapesttram.story: Tram line 2 in Budapest, Hungary, runs beside the Danube past the Parliament. Buda and Pest joined into one city in 1873.

t-viennacafe.title: A café menu board
t-viennacafe.alt: A yellow-tiled café front with lace curtains, a chalk menu board in German and a little serving trolley outside.
t-viennacafe.clue: A coffee house whose chalkboard offers goulash and Sunday concerts, in a capital where coffee-house culture is a listed heritage.
t-viennacafe.story: Café Bräunerhof in Vienna, Austria, holds afternoon concerts at weekends. Viennese coffee-house culture is on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage.

t-hawker.title: A hawker centre
t-hawker.alt: A big open food hall with rows of tables and stools, stalls with signs in English and Chinese, and a woman in a mask in front.
t-hawker.clue: A food hall of cheap stalls with signs in English and Chinese, in a tiny island city-state at the tip of a peninsula.
t-hawker.story: Hawker centres in Singapore were built to move street food stalls indoors. In 2020 hawker culture was added to UNESCO's heritage list.

t-chiangmai.title: Red shared taxis
t-chiangmai.alt: A row of red pickup trucks fitted with roofs and benches, parked by a bus station with signs in a looped script.
t-chiangmai.clue: Red pickup-truck taxis with two benches in the back, in a northern city of hundreds of temples and an old moat.
t-chiangmai.story: The red songthaews of Chiang Mai, Thailand, work like shared taxis: you wave one down and tell the driver where you want to go.

t-mexicocity.title: Workers waiting for jobs
t-mexicocity.alt: Men sitting under umbrellas on a pavement beside a stone church railing, with hand-painted signs offering plumbing, gas and electrical work.
t-mexicocity.clue: Tradesmen wait by a cathedral railing with hand-painted Spanish signs, in a capital built on the site of the Aztec city Tenochtitlan.
t-mexicocity.story: Plumbers, painters and electricians wait for customers outside the Metropolitan Cathedral in Mexico City. They have gathered there for generations.

t-fes.title: A leather tannery
t-fes.alt: Rows of round stone vats filled with brown, red and white dyes, with workers standing among them in an old walled yard.
t-fes.clue: Stone dye vats of a medieval leather tannery, in a car-free walled medina in the north of a land of the Atlas Mountains.
t-fes.story: The Chouara tannery in Fes, Morocco, has worked leather in the same way for about a thousand years. Dyes come from plants such as poppy, indigo and saffron.

t-kualalumpur.title: A covered market street
t-kualalumpur.alt: A busy market street under a glass roof with red lanterns, shops with Chinese signs and stalls of bags and clothes.
t-kualalumpur.clue: A covered Chinatown street of red lanterns and bargain stalls, in a capital whose name means 'muddy confluence'.
t-kualalumpur.story: Petaling Street is the heart of Chinatown in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Its night market sells everything from food to watches.
